passages.text: A song. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. For the choirmaster. According to Mahalath Leannoth. A Maskil of Heman the Ezrahite.
passages.sermon:
This is a song.
This is a psalm.
The sons of Korah wrote this psalm.
The choirmaster will lead this song.
The music follows the tune called Mahalath Leannoth.
This is a maskil, which means it is a teaching psalm.
Heman the Ezrahite wrote this maskil.

passages.text: O LORD, the God of my salvation, day and night I cry out before You.
passages.sermon:
This is a song.
This is a psalm.
The sons of Korah wrote this psalm.
The choirmaster leads this song.
The song is for Mahalath Leannoth.
Heman the Ezrahite wrote this maskil.
LORD, You are the God who saves me.
I cry out to You during the day.
I cry out to You at night.
passages.original: שִׁ֥יר מִזְמ֗וֹר לִבְנֵ֫י קֹ֥רַח לַמְנַצֵּ֣חַ עַל־ מָחֲלַ֣ת לְעַנּ֑וֹת מַ֝שְׂכִּ֗יל לְהֵימָ֥ן הָאֶזְרָחִֽי׃ יְ֭הוָה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יְשׁוּעָתִ֑י יוֹם־ צָעַ֖קְתִּי בַלַּ֣יְלָה נֶגְדֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: May my prayer come before You; incline Your ear to my cry.
passages.sermon:
This is a prayer from Heman the Ezrahite.
He speaks to the LORD.
He asks God to listen.
He says, "Let my prayer come before You."
He says, "Turn Your ear to my cry."
passages.original: תָּב֣וֹא לְ֭פָנֶיךָ תְּפִלָּתִ֑י הַטֵּֽה־ אָ֝זְנְךָ֗ לְרִנָּתִֽי׃

passages.text: For my soul is full of troubles, and my life draws near to Sheol.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks to God.
The psalmist says his soul is full of troubles.
He says his life is close to death.
He feels near to Sheol, the place of the dead.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ שָֽׂבְעָ֣ה בְרָע֣וֹת נַפְשִׁ֑י וְחַיַּ֗י לִשְׁא֥וֹל הִגִּֽיעוּ׃

passages.text: I am counted among those descending to the Pit. I am like a man without strength.
passages.sermon: The speaker is a person who suffers deeply.\r\nPeople count me with those who go down to the Pit.\r\nI am like a man who has no strength.
passages.original: נֶ֭חְשַׁבְתִּי עִם־ י֣וֹרְדֵי ב֑וֹר הָ֝יִ֗יתִי כְּגֶ֣בֶר אֵֽין־ אֱיָֽל׃

passages.text: I am forsaken among the dead, like the slain who lie in the grave, whom You remember no more, who are cut off from Your care.
passages.sermon:
The speaker feels abandoned.
He is among the dead.
He is like those who have been killed.
They lie in the grave.
You do not remember them anymore.
They are cut off from Your care.
passages.original: בַּמֵּתִ֗ים חָ֫פְשִׁ֥י כְּמ֤וֹ חֲלָלִ֨ים׀ שֹׁ֥כְבֵי קֶ֗בֶר אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹ֣א זְכַרְתָּ֣ם ע֑וֹד וְ֝הֵ֗מָּה מִיָּדְךָ֥ נִגְזָֽרוּ׃

passages.text: You have laid me in the lowest Pit, in the darkest of the depths.
passages.sermon: God has placed me in the lowest Pit.\r\nThis Pit is deep and dark.\r\nI am in the darkest depths.

passages.text: Your wrath weighs heavily upon me; all Your waves have submerged me. Selah You have removed my friends from me; You have made me repulsive to them; I am confined and cannot escape.
passages.sermon:
God, You show anger toward me.
Your wrath presses down on me.
You send trouble over me like strong waves.
Your waves cover me completely.
You have taken my friends away from me.
You make me seem disgusting to them.
I am trapped.
I cannot get out.
passages.original: עָ֭לַי סָמְכָ֣ה חֲמָתֶ֑ךָ וְכָל־ מִ֝שְׁבָּרֶ֗יךָ עִנִּ֥יתָ סֶּֽלָה׃ הִרְחַ֥קְתָּ מְיֻדָּעַ֗י מִ֫מֶּ֥נִּי שַׁתַּ֣נִי תוֹעֵב֣וֹת לָ֑מוֹ כָּ֝לֻ֗א וְלֹ֣א אֵצֵֽא׃

passages.text: My eyes grow dim with grief. I call to You daily, O LORD; I spread out my hands to You.
passages.sermon:
I feel deep sorrow.
My eyes grow weak because of my suffering.
I call to You every day, LORD.
I lift my hands to You.
passages.original: עֵינִ֥י דָאֲבָ֗ה מִנִּ֫י עֹ֥נִי קְרָאתִ֣יךָ יְהוָ֣ה בְּכָל־ י֑וֹם שִׁטַּ֖חְתִּי אֵלֶ֣יךָ כַפָּֽי׃

passages.text: Do You work wonders for the dead? Do departed spirits rise up to praise You? Selah Can Your loving devotion be proclaimed in the grave, Your faithfulness in Abaddon ?
passages.sermon:
God, You are powerful.
You can do miracles.
Can You do miracles for the dead?
Do people who have died rise up and praise You?
Can anyone speak about Your love in the grave?
Can anyone tell of Your faithfulness in Abaddon, the place of destruction?
passages.original: הֲלַמֵּתִ֥ים תַּעֲשֶׂה־ פֶּ֑לֶא אִם־ רְ֝פָאִ֗ים יָק֤וּמוּ׀ יוֹד֬וּךָ סֶּֽלָה׃ הַיְסֻפַּ֣ר בַּקֶּ֣בֶר חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ אֱ֝מֽוּנָתְךָ֗ בָּאֲבַדּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Will Your wonders be known in the darkness, or Your righteousness in the land of oblivion?
passages.sermon:
God, You are powerful and righteous.
You do great wonders.
People cannot see in darkness.
People forget in the land of oblivion.
Will anyone know Your wonders in darkness?
Will anyone see Your righteousness in the land of oblivion?
passages.original: הֲיִוָּדַ֣ע בַּחֹ֣שֶׁךְ פִּלְאֶ֑ךָ וְ֝צִדְקָתְךָ֗ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ נְשִׁיָּֽה׃

passages.text: But to You, O LORD, I cry for help; in the morning my prayer comes before You.
passages.sermon:
I am suffering.
I am in despair.
I call to You, LORD.
I cry out for help.
Every morning, I pray to You.
My prayer comes before You at the start of each day.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֤י׀ אֵלֶ֣יךָ יְהוָ֣ה שִׁוַּ֑עְתִּי וּ֝בַבֹּ֗קֶר תְּֽפִלָּתִ֥י תְקַדְּמֶֽךָּ׃

passages.text: Why, O LORD, do You reject me? Why do You hide Your face from me?
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses the LORD.
The speaker feels rejected by the LORD.
The speaker asks the LORD, "Why do You reject me?"
The speaker feels that the LORD hides His face from him.
The speaker asks the LORD, "Why do You hide Your face from me?"
passages.original: לָמָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה תִּזְנַ֣ח נַפְשִׁ֑י תַּסְתִּ֖יר פָּנֶ֣יךָ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

passages.text: From my youth I was afflicted and near death. I have borne Your terrors; I am in despair.
passages.sermon:
I am afflicted.
I have suffered since I was young.
I have been close to death.
I have carried Your terrors.
I am in despair.
passages.original: עָ֘נִ֤י אֲנִ֣י וְגֹוֵ֣עַ מִנֹּ֑עַר נָשָׂ֖אתִי אֵמֶ֣יךָ אָפֽוּנָה׃

passages.text: Your wrath has swept over me; Your terrors have destroyed me.
passages.sermon: Ethan the Ezrahite speaks to the LORD.\r\nHe says, "Your wrath has swept over me."\r\nHe says, "Your terrors have destroyed me."

passages.text: All day long they engulf me like water; they enclose me on every side.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks about his suffering.
He says trouble surrounds him all day.
He feels overwhelmed, like water covers him.
He says these troubles enclose him on every side.
He feels trapped with no escape.
passages.original: סַבּ֣וּנִי כַ֭מַּיִם כָּל־ הַיּ֑וֹם הִקִּ֖יפוּ עָלַ֣י יָֽחַד׃

passages.text: You have removed my beloved and my friend; darkness is my closest companion.
passages.sermon: God, you have taken away my beloved.\r\nYou have taken away my friend.\r\nNow, darkness is my closest companion.
passages.original: הִרְחַ֣קְתָּ מִ֭מֶּנִּי אֹהֵ֣ב וָרֵ֑עַ מְֽיֻדָּעַ֥י מַחְשָֽׁךְ׃
